title: bug: qa_approve and DONE/ARCHIVED moves answer ATTEMPT_FINALIZING with the holder's advice, and finalize_attempt lets any caller follow it
description:
Found by QA of the Wave 1 integration gate (task-808869c5). The gate's adversarial pass did not record it. Code refs are at HEAD 09513e0.

Contract drift between Wave 1 slices:
- task-758423de gave the claim path a refusal worded for QA, `claimEligibility.foreignFinalizingRefusal`. Its own comment (util/claimEligibility.ts:122-124) calls the holder's advice "the wrong advice for a QA caller".
- Two non-holder paths still throw `claimGuards.attemptFinalizingRefusal`: `qa_approve` (tools/qaApprove.ts:79-86) and taskStore.updateTask's DONE/ARCHIVED guard (state/taskStore.ts:265-273, also reached from archive_epic).
- That refusal's message names the attempt id and generation and says "Close the boundary with moe.finalize_attempt, then retry".
- `moe.finalize_attempt` checks only the attempt id/generation fence (tools/finalizeAttempt.ts:204-209) and has no caller or role check. That is by design, so a governor or human can close a dead runner's attempt with outcome 'failed'.

Failure scenario (combined paths, no single slice tests it):
1. The worker calls complete_task. Attempt A goes to finalizing; the row goes to REVIEW, unassigned.
2. A QA agent or governor calls qa_approve {taskId}. An unassigned REVIEW row passes the ownership check.
3. It is refused with A's id and generation, plus the advice to finalize.
4. It calls finalize_attempt {attemptId: A, generation, outcome: 'failed'}, which is accepted.
5. The retried qa_approve succeeds under the default legacy policy, so the task is DONE before its bytes landed.
6. When a qualityGate applies, the wrapper's candidate read finds no open attempt, the "evidence unavailable" path (scripts/moe-agent.sh:1890-1891, 1964-1966; moe-agent.ps1:1281-1296). The completion is parked on a rescue ref that no pre-flight recovers, because a DONE task is never claimed again.

Also stale: util/claimGuards.ts:93, "The refusal both holds raise." attemptFinalizingRefusal now has three non-claim callers (claimNextTask's own-worker hold, qa_approve, the DONE/ARCHIVED guard). The other-seat hold throws foreignFinalizingRefusal instead.
definitionOfDone: qa_approve's and the DONE/ARCHIVED guard's ATTEMPT_FINALIZING refusal addresses a non-holder: wait for the runner to finalize, or close with outcome 'failed' only after confirming the runner is gone. It keeps code -32002, codeName ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, the context keys and retryable:true, and still names the held attempt.
A test per path pins the message and fails on the old holder-voiced text
util/claimGuards.ts:93 comment corrected to the builder's actual callers

implementationPlan.description:
Add the non-holder builder to util/claimGuards.ts, beside attemptFinalizingRefusal, and correct the stale comment.

1. New export:
     export function nonHolderFinalizingRefusal(attempt: FinalizingAttemptRef, action: string): MoeError
   It builds the step-1 message and returns the SAME envelope as attemptFinalizingRefusal: MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT (-32002), codeName ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, and context { attemptId, generation, taskId, workerId, retryable: true } with the same keys in the same order. The only difference is the message, so every existing context assertion keeps passing.
   Its doc comment must say WHY it exists: the holder's advice tells its reader to close the boundary, and a non-holder following that advice closes a live runner's landing, so qa_approve reaches DONE before any byte lands and, under a quality gate, the wrapper finds no open attempt and parks the completion on a rescue ref that no pre-flight recovers, because a DONE task is never claimed again.
2. Correct the comment above attemptFinalizingRefusal (currently 'The refusal both holds raise'). It now has ONE caller: claim_next_task's own-worker hold, the only refused caller whose own runner closes the boundary. Name the two sibling builders and who uses them: nonHolderFinalizingRefusal for qa_approve and for taskStore's DONE/ARCHIVED guard (archive_task, set_task_status and archive_epic all reach it), and claimEligibility.foreignFinalizingRefusal for another seat's claim of the held row.
3. Keep attemptFinalizingRefusal's text exactly as it is: attemptHandback.test.ts pins it for the holder path.
4. claimEligibility.foreignFinalizingRefusal stays as it is too. Its message is claim-specific ('no other seat may claim it') and its tests pin it; three builders with one envelope is the deliberate outcome, and the corrected comment is what keeps them findable.
5. Error handling: the builder only builds an error. It reads no state, cannot throw, and the callers keep raising before any write.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Reuse claimEligibility.foreignFinalizingRefusal for qa_approve and the terminal-column guard: rejected. Its message is claim-specific ('so no other seat may claim it'), and its tests pin that text.
- Give attemptFinalizingRefusal a voice flag: rejected. Every caller would have to pass it, and a missing flag would silently fall back to the wrong voice. A separate named builder makes the wrong choice visible at the call site.
- Add a caller or role check to moe.finalize_attempt: rejected, and out of scope. The open escape is deliberate, so a governor or human can close a dead runner's boundary. The DoD asks to fix the advice, not the permission.
- Unify all three builders into one: rejected here. It would rewrite the claim-path messages that existing tests pin, for no gain on this bug.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- attemptFinalizingRefusal has exactly three callers: claimNextTask's own-worker hold (the holder), qaApprove, and taskStore.assertNoFinalizingAttempt (reached by set_task_status, archive_task and archive_epic).
- claimEligibility.foreignFinalizingRefusal already carries the non-holder voice for a competing claim, and its own comment calls the holder's advice 'the wrong advice for a QA caller'. That is the wording model to follow.
- Existing tests: the holder text is pinned in state/attemptHandback.test.ts ('still refuses the attempt owner its next claim'). The qa_approve hold is covered in tools/finalizeAttempt.test.ts, in the describe 'moe.qa_approve - finalizing hold'. The DONE/ARCHIVED guard and archive_epic are covered in state/attemptHandback.test.ts, with the helper expectHeldForWorker1 pinning the context.
- No doc quotes the message: docs/MCP_SERVER.md only paraphrases it and already tells a refused caller to retry rather than escalate, so no doc change is needed.
- The context envelope is identical across the builders, which is why only the message may change.
planningNotes.risks:
- Do not weaken the existing assertions while adding the message pins. The context, the code and the no-write proofs must stay.
- Keep the envelope identical: same MoeErrorCode, same codeName, same context keys, retryable:true. A client keys on codeName and on context.
- Keep the holder message byte-identical; attemptHandback.test.ts pins it.
- archive_epic must stay atomic: the guard runs up front for every task of the epic, and this change does not move it.
- No in-flight sibling touches these five files (task-31fe6dc8 touches tools/finalizeAttempt.ts but not its test), so no dependsOn is set. Re-check with git status before editing.
